title: response-format negotiator: probe-handshake + streaming syncpoint markers + humanized schema errors
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Enable safer, more debuggable structured-output over streaming while preserving OpenAI-compatibility. Large streaming responses sometimes fail late due to schema violations; apps lose context and users get opaque errors. This change introduces a lightweight negotiation probe (response_format probe) at request start, streaming syncpoint markers for resumable validation checkpoints, and a user-friendly error taxonomy that maps low-level JSONSchema failures to actionable messages and fallback hints.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Add a minimal response_format probe handshake: if client supplies response_format: {type: "json_schema", "mode": "prefer_strict"} the API responds with a small probe confirming supported features (syncpoints, streaming-resume, openai-compat token framing). Probe is sent as the first non-user token in the stream and is optional for backward compatibility.
- Introduce streaming syncpoint markers (internal token: \u003csync:v1 id=UUID\u003e) emitted every N validated objects or bytes; validators anchor to the latest syncpoint to allow the client to safely resume or request a rewind snapshot from the server when recoverable mis-serialization occurs.
- Humanized schema error taxonomy: map common jsonschema failure classes (missing required, type mismatch, additionalProperties) to templated, non-technical messages returned to caller when strict mode is enabled; include suggested mitigation (switch to permissive mode, add missing fields, or use tool-calls to fetch structured data).
- OpenAI-compat adapter changes: honor incoming response_format hints in the OpenAI shim; if probe indicates the downstream does not support syncpoints we degrade to an inline checkpointing approach (embedded JSON fragments).
- Telemetry: emit response.negotiation.* events (probe_sent, probe_response, syncpoint_emitted, validation_failure_{class}) to help investigate regressions.
- Tests: unit tests for probe parsing, integration e2e that validates streaming resume using a simulated flaky model output.

- [x] update OpenAI compat adapter to read response_format hints (adapters/openai/compat.go)
- [x] SDK helper methods for JS/Python (sdk/js/src/responseNegotiator.ts, sdk/python/redwood/response_negotiator.py)

Changed files (high level):
- pkg/api/response_negotiation.go  (new) -- implements probe parse + response payload; small backwards-compatible code paths for clients not sending hints
- pkg/streaming/anchor.go  (new) -- lightweight syncpoint emitter and registry; deliberately small API surface (EmitSyncpoint, LastSyncpoint)
- pkg/validators/schema_validator.go (modified) -- adds failure classification and user-friendly message templates; keeps original validation payloads for debug logs
- adapters/openai/compat.go (modified) -- reads response_format hint header, negotiates probe, and attaches compat fallback when syncpoints are unsupported downstream
- sdk/js/src/responseNegotiator.ts (new) -- client helper to issue probe and parse server probe, expose resume API
- sdk/python/redwood/response_negotiator.py (new) -- same helper for python SDK
- docs/api/response_format.md (new) -- doc describing probe, syncpoints, error classes, and examples for SDKs
- tests/integration/stream_resume_test.go (new) -- simulated flaky server test for resume behavior

Review thread (highlights):
- Lina Chen (review): "Nice taxonomy — can we make the humanized messages opt-in (so enterprise customers can retain raw errors for internal tooling)?"
  - Asha: "Added a per-tenant flag 'response.errors.humanize' (defaults to true for public API) and a SDK toggle; docs updated."
- Diego Morales (review): "Adapter fallback looks correct. Two nit: move compat fallback code to a helper and add a comment about payload ordering when probe is absent."
  - Asha: "Moved fallback to compat helper, left an explicit comment. PTAL."
- Ethan Park (review): "Test coverage looks good; e2e flaky model test catches resume path. One concern: emitting too-frequent syncpoints might increase token count. Could we default to 4KB or 5 objects?"
  - Asha: "Defaulted to 4KB / 5 objects, configurable via runtime config; added note in telemetry.md about tradeoffs."

- Plan to expose a lightweight SDK event when a validation failure triggers an automatic server fallback to permissive mode so clients can log sampling metrics (PM-381).

User-facing examples (in docs/api/response_format.md):
Request hint header: "X-Redwood-Response-Format: {\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"mode\":\"prefer_strict\",\"probe\":true}"
Server probe (first event in stream): "{\"probe\":{\"syncpoints\":true,\"resumable\":true,\"compat_openai_frame\":true}}"
Syncpoint token (internal): "\u003csync:v1 id=1a2b3c4d-...\u003e"
Humanized error example returned when strict mode fails: "Response validation failed: the model omitted required field 'due_date'. Consider switching to permissive mode or adding 'due_date' to the schema. More: /docs/response_format#errors"

Release notes:
- Add response_format probe handshake and streaming syncpoints for resumable validation
- Add humanized JSON schema error taxonomy and SDK helpers
- OpenAI-compat adapter honors response_format hints and falls back gracefully
